The user is asking about a JWT expiry check bug in Express middleware. Caveman mode is active (default: full).

The issue: JWT `exp` field is in **seconds** since epoch, but `Date.now()` returns **milliseconds**. So `Date.now() > token.exp` will almost always be true... wait, actually it means the token NEVER appears expired because `Date.now()` (e.g., 1700000000000) is always much larger than `exp` (e.g., 1700000000). So the check `Date.now() < token.exp` would always pass (token always looks valid), letting expired tokens through.
 
The bug is almost certainly `Date.now() < token.exp` since milliseconds are vastly larger than seconds—this comparison always evaluates true, so expired tokens slip through. The fix is to normalize the units by dividing `Date.now()` by 1000.
